what: [designed: T153] Done-when 2 on Windows, driven headlessly by drive_first_run.py (its docstring says what each phase clicks)
interpreter: the build's python\python.exe (console, for the log; goal2.cmd uses pythonw.exe) running goal2_launch.main from the build root, so the launcher's environment and runpy -m goal2.desktop are the build's
environment: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy; LOCALAPPDATA set to the run folder's local\ so the owner's real %LOCALAPPDATA%\goal2 stays fresh for the playtest

phases.first: no arguments: import dialog; an empty folder refused naming both files; the owner's folder imported; Launch New career (Denmark, 1992, 'T Fiftythree'), bulletins, main window; one round played watched through CoreModel.round_step (4402 steps: captain, 4396 live polls, half time, 2 replay prompts declined, full time, summary declined); Save button; window closed
phases.second: no arguments: no dialog; Launch shows the saved career DENMARK
phases.resume: --resume <saves>\desktop.g2core: main window, memory sha256 equal to the saved one
phases.launch-resume: no arguments: Launch's Resume button (RESUME DENMARK, #519): main window, memory sha256 equal to the saved one

not_driven: the window's own round page and the pygame pitch viewer (the round was played through the same model calls without them); real mouse/keyboard input
note: engine_python in the logs is read before the launcher sets GOAL2_ENGINE_PYTHON, hence null; the core round runs in the core, not in a PyPy worker
